name: REBUILD Strategist Original Decision-Centric Marketing Agent OS
implemented: original methodology and phase gates (documented)
deterministic state machine with rollback transitions
JSON Schema validator (stdlib): type/required/properties/additionalProperties/items/enum/ranges/anyOf/oneOf/allOf; unimplemented keywords are reported rather than silently ignored
evidence ledger: validated JSONL append, semantic quality checks, gap analysis, machine-checkable provenance ratio, Markdown export
data sources: local files (CSV/TSV/JSON/JSONL/TXT/MD/XLSX with CJK encoding fallback) and user-supplied HTTP endpoints; SHA-256 provenance; secrets read from environment only
runtime orchestrator: sequential per-phase role dispatch, evidence and material injection, model-judged gates, state-machine-adjudicated transitions, schema-validated decision record
decision store: persist decisions, surface overdue reviews proactively, back-fill outcomes with mandatory deviation typing (execution/strategy/assumption/mixed/unknown), write back to project.json
6 JSON Schemas enforced: project, evidence, decision, decision outcome, experiment, KPI tree
8 differentiated specialist role contracts
DeepSeek Harness skill and installation guide (harness/)
blind-review harness: hashed ids, shuffled order, identity hiding, reviewer agreement check
model provider layer (OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible)
scorecard structural validation (totals vs dimensions, value ranges, required fields)
unit tests (297, passing on Python 3.10-3.13; 2 provider tests require >=3.10)
a complete real-project case, anonymized, with reproducible analysis scripts (examples/metro_apartment/)
GitHub Actions CI workflow for Python 3.10-3.13, including an end-to-end smoke test
community health files: SECURITY, CODE_OF_CONDUCT, PR and Issue templates
anonymization guard in CI: generic leak patterns (company names, street numbers, transit stations, policy numbers, local paths) for the published real-project case
per-phase gate criteria (each REBUILD phase judged against its own standard from REBUILD_METHOD.md)
three-tier gate verdict: SUFFICIENT / DEGRADED (must declare limitations) / INSUFFICIENT
validated end-to-end against a real model (DeepSeek deepseek-chat): forward, rollback and blocking paths all exercised
orchestrator fault-path handling, covered by tests: single role failure, all roles failing, gate exceptions, truncated JSON, decision-record failure, unknown provider failing fast
multi-run comparison (core/compare.py): deterministic process reproducibility (paths, final states, gate grades, count spread) kept strictly separate from model-judged conclusion agreement
token usage capture per model call (facts only; missing usage is reported as incomplete, never estimated)
cost estimation from user-supplied unit prices, reported separately from token counts with an explicit 'not a bill' caveat
decision outcome back-fill used on a real project for the first time (examples/metro_apartment/decisions/)
AS_EXPECTED deviation type: a review that finds no deviation is a legitimate conclusion, not UNKNOWN
not_implemented: parallel multi-agent dispatch (the orchestrator is strictly sequential: one role, one model call)
built-in marketing platform connectors (deliberately excluded; the data layer accepts only user-provided files or endpoints)
decision history versioning and dependency rollback (assumptions being refuted does not yet auto-list affected decisions)
execution of marketing actions (the system produces decisions and validation plans; it does not advertise, message, or write back to any external system)
partial: benchmark experiment: one pilot run only (case B03, n=1 per config, 1 of 4 cases). Sample size is far below the standard set by bench/RUBRIC.md and does NOT constitute comparative evidence. See bench/PILOT_B03.md.

real-world outcome of the published case: the recommendation was adopted and the predicted blocker (the operator refusing the 65/35 split) materialised, but the REVISED split has not been modelled and no operating data exists yet. Adoption is not validation.
unverified: end-to-end quality in any host environment
comparative quality against plain prompts or single-skill setups
independence and provenance of the two pilot reviewers (no record kept)
whether the method generalises beyond one real project (a single anonymised case now exists; one case is not a sample)
whether decision reviews actually happen on schedule in a real project (the mechanism exists; nobody has used it yet)
commercial value hypotheses: consulting delivery, corporate training, evaluation layer
real-world ROI impact in commercial projects
the absolute quality of orchestrator output against a real model (it runs end-to-end; whether the analysis is good needs independent review)
orchestrator behaviour under API faults (429, timeout, truncated or non-JSON responses)
a real commercial project completing the full loop (the real case correctly blocks at R; E-U-I-D were exercised on a constructed test project)

run-to-run stability: same input, temperature 0, three runs all reached a 'validate first' conclusion but differed 2.5x in the number of falsification conditions; temperature 0 does not remove the variance
whether the model-judged conclusion-agreement verdict is itself reliable (it is a model judgement, not a fact, and is subject to the same variance)
measured cost of a full loop: 16 calls / ~92k tokens / ~2 minutes; the dollar figure depends entirely on the unit price the user supplies
